title: Version-only vulnerability claim contradicts a verified backported fix
description: The finding agent inferred a template-rendering vulnerability from the server's ExampleRenderer/1.2.0 banner. This synthetic deployment intentionally retains that banner for compatibility while running a patched build. The specific claimed template-expression path was checked and does not evaluate the supplied expression.
exploitation_steps: Read the ExampleRenderer/1.2.0 banner in the isolated test deployment and flag it using the test scanner's version-only rule.
Inspect the deployment build manifest and the actual template handler to check whether the claimed vulnerable evaluation path is present.
Submit the benign template marker {{ 7 * 7 }} through the claimed route. Observe that it is returned as literal text rather than evaluated to 49.
Run the same input against a disposable unpatched fixture and observe evaluation to 49, confirming that the test distinguishes the patched and unpatched behavior.
impact: The agent claims server-side template execution solely from the version banner. The deployed handler has the relevant fix, and the reproduced request shows the expression remains inert. No server-side expression execution, data access, or other adverse security consequence was demonstrated through the reported route.
evidence: Synthetic banner: ExampleRenderer/1.2.0. Synthetic deployment manifest: build=1.2.0+security.3; patch=render-user-input-as-text; the banner string is configured separately from the build identifier.

Deployed handler review: user input is passed to the template as a text variable; it is not compiled or evaluated as a template. The vulnerable handler exists only in the disposable unpatched comparison fixture.
Patched-route response contains the literal string {{ 7 * 7 }}; the unpatched comparison fixture returns 49 for the identical input.
The initial scanner report contains only a banner match, with no exploit observation contradicting the deployed handler review or the controlled comparison.

context.environment: Entirely fictional renderer, scanner rule, build identifiers, and authorized test fixtures; no real product or advisory is referenced
context.intended_policy: User template content must be treated as inert text
context.attacker_access: Public banner visibility and access to the user-text rendering route
context.known_mitigations: The specific vulnerable evaluation path is replaced by text-variable rendering in the deployed build
context.scope_of_evidence: The claimed template-evaluation bug and route were checked; the unchanged banner does not establish unrelated vulnerabilities
